findings.message: Authenticated public check public-C01 failed with exit_code 1: for input '# ##' the expected title is '' but the observed title is '##' (actual vs expected mismatch in the fixed public case set). The other three fixed cases passed: '# C#' -> 'C#', '# C# #' -> 'C#', '# Title #' -> 'Title'. A known public mismatch is a contract failure.

Root cause of the observed failure: the candidate closer alternative '(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)' only fires when a non-space character immediately precedes the separator. For a terminal hash run following an empty title (e.g. '# ##', '# #', '#  ##') the character before the separator is the space after the marker, the lookbehind fails, and the hashes are captured as literal title text instead of being removed as a separated closer. This regresses the baseline behavior, which yielded '' for '# ##'.

Scope confirmation: the diff is a single-line change to _ATX_HEADING_PATTERN inside MarkdownFile; _FENCE_PATTERN, _parse_headings, _build_section, find_heading and find_section are byte-identical to the baseline, so fence exclusion, levels, line numbers, hierarchy boundaries and lookup semantics are untouched by the change.

However, the authenticated public check public-C01 failed (exit_code 1): for input '# ##' the expected title is '' (empty title, with the separated terminal hash run treated as a closer, matching the baseline) but the candidate observed '##'. Mechanism (inference): the closer alternative '(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)' requires a non-space character immediately before the separator, so a terminal hash run following an empty title cannot be recognized as a closer and is instead captured into the text group; the same class affects '# #' and '#  ##'. This regresses the baseline's trimming/separated-closer/empty-title behavior, violating the task's preservation requirement and the current-owner title-contract obligation. Disposition: reject.
